transcript.text: Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I can certainly help with that. The most common reason a washing machine won't spin is that it hasn't drained the water first; the machine will refuse to spin if there is still water in the drum. This is often caused by a blockage in the pump filter, which is easy to check and usually free to fix. Please locate the small flap at the bottom front of your machine, open it, and unscrew the filter (have some towels ready for any water). Let me know if you find anything blocked or if the filter was clear.
its drained fine, no water in the drum. it was just one big bath mat that came out dripping wet. do i still need to do the filter?

You do not need to check the filter right now. The machine has successfully drained, so the blockage isn't stopping the spin cycle. The fact that you washed a single large bath mat is the most likely cause here. Washing machines struggle to balance heavy, absorbent items like mats or duvets; they tend to stick to one side of the drum, causing the machine to abort the high-speed spin to prevent damage. This is normal behaviour for this type of load. To confirm this isn't a deeper fault with the motor or suspension, please take the mat out and run a 'spin-only' programme with an empty drum. Does it spin up properly when there is nothing inside?
not sure how to do a spin only tbh, which programme is that? the full load yesterday spun fine tho

It is usually called 'Spin Only' or 'Rinse & Spin'. Look for a button labelled 'Spin' or turn the dial to the position marked with just a spin symbol (often one or two water drops). Select that and start it. Does the drum spin up properly when empty?
ok i see a rinse & spin on the dial i think. but tbh the full load yesterday spun fine so is it really needed with an empty drum?

It is not strictly needed if you are happy to wash that mat separately next time, but running an empty spin suggests whether the machine's drive and suspension are healthy. Given the dripping wet mat, the most likely cause is simply that the heavy item soaked up water and stuck to one side, causing the machine to abort the spin for safety. This is normal behaviour for bulky items. If you do try the empty spin and it works fine, you can just wash the mat alone next time with a few towels to balance it.
